a→q, b→w, c→e, d→r, e→t, f→y, g→u, h→i, i→o,
j→p, k→a, l→s, m→d, n→f, o→g, p→h, q→j, r→k,
s→l, t→z, u→x, v→c, w→v, x→b, y→n, z→m
```

These are exactly the letters of the keyboard‑order alphabet  

```
"qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm"
```

so each input letter is replaced by the letter in the same position of that
string (a → first letter, b → second, …, z → twenty‑sixth).

The required function therefore builds this mapping and translates the
input string character‑by‑character.
